review.derivation: Two four-carbon arms meet the carbon bonded to a two-carbon ethenyl arm. Modern longest parent: 4+1+4=9 carbons, ethenyl at 5. Historical parent containing C=C: 2+1+4=7, double bond at 1 and butyl at 3.
Same three-arm graph as the preceding case, with a triple bond. Nine-carbon modern parent has ethynyl at 5; seven-carbon historical unsaturated parent has triple bond at 1 and butyl at 3.
Unbranched six-carbon chain with three alternating double bonds at 1,3,5. The a connecting vowel precedes triene; locants move before the parent in the recorded historical convention.
Five-carbon chain with C1#C2 and C4#C5, equivalent directions, a retained before diyne. Historical locants precede parent.
Six-carbon chain; OH at C3 rather than C4 controls direction despite C=C receiving C4 rather than C2.
OH lies on an external two-carbon chain. Parent containing suffix OH is ethan-1-ol; the separate six-carbon ring is cyclohexyl at C2.
Five-carbon unbranched chain; carbonyl is assigned C2 rather than C4, placing C=C at C3. Terminal e of ene is elided before one.
Seven-carbon ring, carbonyl C1. Double-bond sets 2,4 and 4,6 select 2,4. Modern locants separate parent/ene/one; A-11.3 and C-314.1 give historical adienone with carbonyl C1 implicit.
Eight-carbon ring with one ring ketone, numbered from carbonyl C1. Double bonds at 2,4,6 are preferred to 3,5,7. Historical a+trienone retains C1 as the inherent ketone position.
COOH carbon is outside the saturated six-carbon ring; carboxylic acid is appended to cyclohexane without counting that carbon as a seventh ring atom.
Nitrile carbon lies outside a saturated six-carbon ring. The ring parent takes carbonitrile rather than counting the CN carbon in the ring.
Three-carbon acyl chain includes carbonyl as C1; the ethyl group attaches to nitrogen and must receive an N locant.
Longest carbon group directly attached to N is propyl, making propan-1-amine. The two remaining methyl groups attach to N and require N,N locants.
HO-CH2-CH2-CONH2 is the explicit P-41 example: amide is senior to alcohol; carbonyl carbon is C1 and hydroxy is at C3.
OHC-CH2-CH2-CN is the explicit P-41 example: nitrile is senior to aldehyde. Nitrile carbon is C1, aldehyde oxygen is represented by oxo at C4.
Four-carbon acid chain includes the carboxyl carbon as C1; ketone at C3 becomes oxo. Carboxylic acid is senior to ketone.
Three-carbon acid parent, carboxyl at C1, hydroxyl at C3; acid suffix and hydroxy prefix.
Unbranched four-carbon chain, terminal CHO is C1; the secondary hydroxyl is at C3 and is a hydroxy prefix.
Five-carbon chain counted from aldehyde carbon C1. Internal ketone carbon is C4 and contributes oxo, because aldehyde is senior.
Four-carbon chain; suffix ketone receives C2 rather than C3, placing subordinate hydroxy at C3.
